{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement (Exhibit 10.14)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** Legal (in-house counsel to Customer / AP) 
**Re:** Playbook review of the Kubient Master Services Agreement dated 5 February 
**Status:** All findings below are verified (verification: pass).

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against 19 playbook rules. Thirteen clauses are compliant, three are deviations requiring redlines, and three rules have no usable clause in the document at all.

The commercial architecture is favourable to us in the areas that usually cause the most trouble. There is no exclusivity, no non-compete, no MFN, no minimum commitment, no non-solicit and no audit right running against us; Section 1 expressly confirms we remain free to offer or sell Inventory through other agents or third parties. The vendor-side indemnity at Section 11 is broad, procedurally sound and uncapped in practice, and the Section 9(b) performance warranty runs for the whole Term, which is better than our preferred position. Assignment, termination for convenience and governing law all sit at or above the fallback and are not redlined.

Three issues need to be raised with the counterparty. First, and most significant, Section 7 waives consequential damages but contains **no monetary cap of any kind**, leaving our direct liability unlimited; because this is a revenue-share deal in which we pay no fees to Kubient, a "fees paid" cap would be illusory, so we propose the greater-of formulation with a USD 1,000,000 floor plus standard uncapped carve-outs. Second, the Section 2 platform licence is expressly "revocable" without qualifier and runs to Customer alone, with Section 6(a) barring third-party access absent Kubient's prior written consent — so Affiliates and contractors are excluded and the licence could be pulled at will. Third, the only post-Initial-Term exit is a 90-day notice, which exceeds our 60-day fallback ceiling.

Three rules are unaddressed: there is no IP/ownership article allocating our Content, Requests or visitor data; Section 4(c) permits each party to "return or destroy" the other's Confidential Information with no transition assistance or data-return right; and there is no insurance covenant at all, notwithstanding that Kubient hosts the platform and, on its own warranty, collects and stores visitor data.

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | Preamble (Section 11) |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | **Deviation** | Preamble (Section 7) |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | Preamble (Section 14(h)) |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | Preamble (Section 1) |
| High | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Missing** | Preamble |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | Preamble (Sections 4(a), 5) |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | Preamble (Sections 2, 6(a)) |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | Preamble (Section 1) |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant (at fallback) | Preamble (Section 4(a)) |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | Preamble |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant (law at fallback) | Preamble (Section 14(a)) |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Compliant | Preamble (Section 1) |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | Preamble (Sections 1, 5) |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | Preamble |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | **Deviation** | Preamble (Section 4(a)) |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | Preamble (Section 4(c)) |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant (exceeds preferred) | Preamble (Sections 9(b), 13) |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | Preamble (Section 14) |

### Deviations and gaps — what we changed and why

**LOL-CAP (critical, deviation — Section 7).** Section 7 is a mutual consequential-damages waiver carved out for indemnification and breach of confidentiality, but no cap on direct liability appears anywhere in the document. The fallback requires a mutual 12-months'-fees cap with carve-outs, so the total absence of a cap fails on a material term. Our redline adds a mutual cap on the preferred greater-of basis using amounts paid or payable between the Parties with a USD 1,000,000 floor, adds the standard uncapped carve-outs, and confirms revenue-share amounts owed are not "damages" for cap purposes. The existing mutual waiver is acceptable and is left intact.

**LICENSE (high, deviation — Sections 2 and 6(a)).** The grant is expressly "revocable" with no qualifier, so on its face Kubient may withdraw the licence at will mid-Term, and it runs to "Customer" alone while Section 6(a) bars third-party access without Kubient's prior written consent — leaving Affiliate and contractor access to Kubient's discretion, contrary to the fallback (Affiliates covered on written notice). Our redline extends the grant to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, confirms such access is not prohibited third-party access (with us responsible for their compliance), and limits revocation to expiration or termination under Section 4. Successor transfer is already handled by Section 14(h) and is preserved.

**RENEWAL (medium, deviation — Section 4(a)).** Renewal terms are successive one-year periods, which is acceptable, but the only post-Initial-Term exit is a 90-day notice, exceeding the 60-day fallback ceiling. Our redline shortens the notice to 30 days and confirms it may be exercised as a non-renewal election; we can settle at 60 days. Pricing is a revenue share with no unilateral uplift mechanic, so the CPI/3% cap is not engaged.

**IP (high, missing).** There is no ownership article. The only ownership-adjacent language is Kubient's warranty that it owns the IP in the Service, Auction Platform and products delivered, our warranty that we own the Content and Properties, and a trademark-only provision — none of which allocates ownership of our Content, Requests or visitor data, assigns deliverables, or excludes joint ownership, while Kubient collects and stores visitor data and receives Requests with no use limitation. We have inserted a new General Provisions (j): we retain all rights in our Content, Properties and data; Kubient keeps its platform and pre-existing tools; deliverables created for us are assigned to us with a perpetual, royalty-free licence to embedded Kubient IP; no joint ownership. Note there is no assignment of our IP or data to Kubient, so this is a gap rather than a walk-away.

**TRANSITION (medium, missing — Section 4(c)).** On termination Kubient simply ceases the Services, the licence is revoked, and each Party may "return or destroy" the other's Confidential Information at its own election — with no transition assistance, no right to receive our data back in a usable format and no deletion certification. We have inserted a new paragraph 4(c)(v) at the preferred position: up to six months' assistance at then-current rates, machine-readable return within 30 days, then deletion with written certification, expressly overriding the destroy option for Customer Data. Fallback of 90 days' assistance with export within 30 days is flagged in the comment.

**INSURANCE (low, missing — Section 14).** The Agreement contains no insurance requirement, yet Kubient hosts the Auction Platform and on its own warranty collects, maintains and stores visitor data. We have inserted a short covenant as new Section 14(j) at preferred levels (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request), with the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) offered in the comment.

## Walk-away items

Three points reach or approach walk-away territory under the playbook and should not be conceded without escalation:

1. **Licence revocable at will (Section 2).** An unqualified revocation right is walk-away territory; revocation must be limited to expiration or termination under Section 4.
2. **No data return on termination (Section 4(c)).** Because Kubient may elect destruction of our Confidential Information, this sits at or near the walk-away position of no data return / immediate deletion, and fails even the fallback. A machine-readable return right is required.
3. **No insurance where the vendor processes personal data (Section 14).** A hosting vendor that collects and stores visitor data with no coverage requirement is the walk-away scenario under the insurance rule.

For completeness, the uncapped direct liability under Section 7 is not itself a stated walk-away, but as a critical deviation that leaves our own exposure unlimited it should be treated as a must-fix.

## Next steps

1. Issue the redline covering the three deviations (LOL-CAP, LICENSE, RENEWAL) and the three insertions (IP ownership as General Provisions (j), transition/data return as Section 4(c)(v), insurance as Section 14(j)), with fallbacks noted in comments.
2. Confirm negotiating priority: liability cap and licence revocability first, then data return and insurance; the 90-to-30-day renewal notice is our most tradeable item (settle at 60 days).
3. **Review the Exhibits as executed.** Fee terms sit in Exhibits not included in this review. If any Exhibit introduces an early-termination or shortfall payment by us, it should be capped at three months' fees per the LD fallback; if any Exhibit introduces committed volumes or spend, MINCOMMIT must be re-run.
4. Raise with the deal team the reporting gap noted under AUDIT: Impressions are measured solely "as measured by Kubient" and revenue share is per Exhibit with no verification right on our side. We recommend seeking a reporting/revenue-verification right in our favour — this is additive to our position rather than a deviation.
5. If drafting is reopened, align the Section 8 AAA arbitration provision with the exclusive court jurisdiction in Section 14(a). The arbitration is AAA-administered and domestic, so it does not reach the foreign-seat walk-away, and Delaware law sits at the fallback; neither point justifies a standalone redline."}
